summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs. Enforcement persists across the required node reboot; CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the locked-password local opsadmin account.
Installed /etc/cron.allow containing exactly root and opsadmin, owned by root:root with mode 0644.
Verified root and opsadmin can create, list, and remove crontabs while antrieb is denied.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified a changed boot identity, recovered crond service, persistent configuration, and post-reboot enforcement.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: The allowlist contains exactly root and opsadmin. Both allowed users successfully exercised crontab; antrieb was denied before and after reboot.
opsadmin exists as UID/GID 501 with /bin/bash and a locked password; the account persisted after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained

evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot ID and healthy state were captured; reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect; boot ID changed from 99bde3c2-c1f1-46b0-8000-000000000000 to 453830a0-18d3-402f-8000-000000000000; crond, accounts, allowlist, and enforcement recovered.
